summary: The core ~3000-line document underlying the surrounding kernel-minimality review chain: defines a semantic environment 8-tuple, semantic trace, observational and semantic equivalence (with a proof obligation that equiv_sem is itself an equivalence relation), capability simulation via a Beh(K) behavior-set with the critical equiv_sem != equiv_cap distinction, a preorder-then-quotiented-partial-order capability ordering, capability derivability and an experimental-vs-mathematical irreducibility split, completeness, semantic minimality, existence, uniqueness, a full minimality theorem with proof idea, a statistics evidence ladder, DDD ownership/no-capability-laundering/system-composition extensions, a capability-identity/granularity problem, a formalized counterfactual capability restriction K^{-c}, and a three-way capability/implementation/architectural minimality distinction; its closing section (from 'The four new additions are genuinely important' onward) duplicates S2674 verbatim.
contribution_assessment: This is the richest single document in the kernel-minimality thread, introducing the semantic environment and trace apparatus that all later reviews (S2669-S2674) build on and correct: the Beh(K)-based capability simulation with its explicit equiv_sem-vs-equiv_cap distinction, the preorder-to-partial-order-by-quotient move, a rigorous minimality theorem with a clean proof-by-contradiction idea, an explicit empirical-evidence-vs-formal-proof discipline, DDD ownership/no-laundering/system-composition formalizations, the capability-identity ambiguity problem (is 'Determine' the same capability as 'SelectAnswer'?), the granularity problem (Interpret'={Observe,Interpret} making Determine's irreducibility vocabulary-dependent), a formalized counterfactual capability restriction K^{-c} (the actual origin of the concept later reviewed in S2674), and a three-way distinction between capability, implementation, and architectural minimality that keeps operator-count optimization permanently out of scope.

summary: Accepts the prior kernel-minimality review as the basis for the next formal artifact, freezing eight already-established principles (counterfactual removal, relative minimality, capability-identity-before-basis, transition-primary equivalence, contract-relative losslessness, K_adm/K_sat separation, DDD responsibility projection, parallel empirical/formal tracks), then adds one further correction: capability itself should not yet be defined as a four-field tuple but via an intermediate Cap_C(K) abstraction (the contract-distinguishable semantic contribution of K), with a specific representation chosen only afterward, and freezes a fourteen-stage proof dependency graph.
contribution_assessment: Mostly consolidates prior corrections already captured in S2669-S2675, but adds one genuinely new refinement: before committing to any specific capability representation (e.g. the four-field tuple (I_c,O_c,Gamma_c,Inv_c)), first ask whether a capability is a behavior, relation, transformation class, or equivalence class of such objects, introducing an intermediate abstraction Cap_C(K) (the contract-distinguishable semantic contribution of K) to avoid smuggling a premature ontology; also freezes the full fourteen-stage dependency graph for the next proof artifact.

summary: Confirms the accumulated kernel-minimality review as the approved proof-design specification (not Theory v1.3), reframing the research question from 'what Kernel operators should we choose' to 'what mathematical object is a semantic capability', and adds a circularity guard instructing the future formal-proof agent to stop and expose any definition that depends on arbitrary capability naming or decomposition.
contribution_assessment: Adds one new governance instruction for the eventual formal-proof agent -- if any definition depends on arbitrary naming or decomposition of the candidate capabilities, stop and expose the circularity rather than proceeding -- as a single rule meant to protect the whole proof from recreating the 13->12->8 operator-counting problem; otherwise confirms the twelve-stage dependency chain and reaffirms Theory v1.2 stays frozen pending KR-KERNEL-EQUIVALENCE-CAPABILITY-PROOF-2026-09.

summary: A literature search connecting KnowledgeOS to established mathematical traditions -- Kohlas/Shenoy Information Algebra, Plotkin's algebraic knowledge-base informational equivalence, Cirulis's algebraic belief system, and epistemic algebra -- finding no existing framework matches the full KnowledgeOS Kernel+Zero+representation-reduction programme, reframing Zero as a quotient-induced eliminability predicate (D\x equiv_{T,Pi} D) rather than an algebraic zero element, proposing a layered (not monolithic) Knowledge Algebra architecture, and recommending a new three-sub-lane research programme KR-ALGEBRA (Information Algebra, Knowledge Algebra, Zero Algebra, with Zero depending on the other two).
contribution_assessment: Grounds the KnowledgeOS Zero/Kernel research in real prior mathematical literature for the first time: Information Algebra's combine/focus operations closely parallel the Zero question; Plotkin's informational equivalence of knowledge bases is a legitimate precedent for the project's own semantic-equivalence definition, though narrower than KnowledgeOS's implementation-level equivalence; distinguishes ordinary algebraic zero (additive identity/absorbing element) from the project's Zero as a counterfactual observational-equivalence judgment, closer to sufficient statistics, bisimulation, and database dependency theory; proposes reformalizing Zero via an explicit observational quotient F_{T,Pi}(D)=Pi(T(D)) with ten concrete follow-up mathematical questions (equivalence-relation status, quotient structure, congruence, compositionality, idempotence, order-independence, normal form, algebra-admission, reconstructibility); and issues an explicit warning against branding this 'Knowledge Algebra' before a serious prior-art map is done.

summary: A full 56-page reading of Kenneth Williams's 'Vedic Math Genius', extracting structural transformation patterns (reference-relative representation, compensation, complement/involution, local-plus-interaction decomposition, carrying as state propagation, duplex/interaction terms, deficiency, scale transformation, execution-order independence, state cycles in recurring decimals, residual-carrying transformations, representation-changing 'negative flag', representative-value abstraction, five distinct zero-like mechanisms, closure/completion, sufficient local statistics, invariants/checksums, combinatorial composition), reclassifying all sixteen sutras structurally, proposing a new hypothesis KR-ALGEBRA-H1 (a representation-relative transformation algebra where Zero emerges rather than being primitive), a ten-property experiment KR-ALGEBRA-01, ten philosophical inspiration points, and a historical-claims-vs-mathematical-evidence caution, concluding with a three-sub-lane KR-ALGEBRA research programme.
contribution_assessment: The deepest single-book structural analysis in the corpus: identifies five distinct zero-like Vedic mechanisms (cancellation, residual disappearance, proportional explanation, completion, complement) that must not be collapsed, reclassifies all sixteen named sutras into structural transformation families, proposes a seven-part candidate algebra A_K=(K,R,T,Q,equiv,I,E) in which Zero emerges from the structure rather than being primitive, specifies a concrete ten-property test battery (compensation, involution, idempotence, interaction, reference/residual decomposition, question-relative sufficiency, invariant preservation, order independence, normalization) for the new KR-ALGEBRA-01 experiment, and ends with an explicit historical-claim-versus-mathematical-evidence discipline plus a three-sub-lane KR-ALGEBRA programme (Representation/Transformation/Observational-Zero Algebra).

summary: A more radical, structure-not-shortcut re-reading of the Vedic material, culminating in the batch's most important new Zero formalization: an explicit observation-induced quotient (D1~D2 iff Pi(T(D1))=Pi(T(D2))) under which Zero becomes equality of equivalence classes [D]=[E_x(D)], a six-level Zero hierarchy Z0-Z5 (mathematical zero through algebraic zero) placing KnowledgeOS Zero at Z3/Z4 not Z5, an explicit congruence test for whether the quotient inherits an algebraic operation, a Knowledge-Kernel-orthogonal-to-Knowledge-Algebra architecture, and a new experiment named KR-ALGEBRA-01 ('Quotient and Zero Structure') that collides in name with a differently-scoped KR-ALGEBRA-01 ('Transformation Property Discovery') proposed in an earlier file of this same batch.
contribution_assessment: Contributes the sharpest mathematical formalization of Zero in the whole Vedic-inspired research lane: reframes Zero via an explicit observation-induced quotient and a six-level hierarchy (Z0 ordinary algebraic zero, Z1 expression cancellation, Z2 transformational eliminability, Z3 observational Zero, Z4 quotient Zero, Z5 algebraic zero), explicitly placing the currently-evidenced KnowledgeOS Zero at Z3/Z4, never Z5; specifies the congruence test needed before any quotient can inherit an algebraic operation; separates Knowledge Kernel from Knowledge Algebra as orthogonal in semantic responsibility, not mathematical structure; and designs a ten-step experiment (also named KR-ALGEBRA-01, distinct from and colliding in name with the S2681 KR-ALGEBRA-01) to test the quotient, congruence, commutativity of elimination, idempotence, and normal-form convergence.

summary: A rigorous formal-mathematics pass on Vedic Math Genius, translating five Williams procedures into exact abstract algebra (ring-shifted distributive law, b's-complement involution, Cauchy convolution for polynomial multiplication, symmetry-reduced self-convolution for duplex squaring, DFA orbits over finite multiplicative groups for recurring decimals), proving the divisibility-by-4 example is a genuine minimal sufficient statistic via the data-processing inequality, and delivering a critical complexity-theory reality check that Vedic methods do not change asymptotic complexity class (Theta(n^2), inferior to Karatsuba/FFT) -- their benefit is human working-memory reduction only -- before freezing a formal KR-ALGEBRA-DISCOVERY-2026-09 register entry.
contribution_assessment: Supplies the rigorous mathematical grounding the prior Vedic-algebra discussions lacked: exact ring/polynomial/finite-field translations for five procedures, a complete data-processing-inequality proof that the divisibility-by-4 statistic is minimally sufficient, and -- most importantly -- an explicit asymptotic-complexity table proving Vedic methods never change complexity class and only reduce human working-memory load, directly refuting a common overclaim about Vedic Mathematics; also delivers a frozen KR-ALGEBRA-DISCOVERY-2026-09 register entry with a translation table, the candidate transformation family A_K, the 10 verification axioms, a refined five-way Knowledge Zero classification, and the admission stopping rule.

summary: Reads the Atharva Veda as a structural-prior source for DDD-style epistemic separation of concerns (Representation/Inquiry/Evidence/Determination/Transformation/Revision/Elimination/Truth as distinct responsibilities), introduces a 'semantic ownership' invariant preventing any context from silently redefining another's invariant, reformulates Zero via a Contribution function and as derived from an observation-induced equivalence, distinguishes three kinds of zero (algebraic, structural, observational), proposes an eleven-item broader algebraic vocabulary and a four-sub-lane KR-ALGEBRA research programme plus a separate KR-KERNEL lane, and specifies a six-experiment KR-ALGEBRA-01 protocol (equivalence, congruence, interaction, residual, elimination order, normal form/confluence) that is the third document in this batch to reuse the name 'KR-ALGEBRA-01' for a differently-scoped experiment.
contribution_assessment: Introduces genuinely new architectural material: a 'semantic ownership' function and invariant (no bounded context may silently redefine another's invariant -- Representation cannot redefine truth, Zero cannot redefine knowledge, Governance cannot become truth), a purification-as-transformation-not-state distinction (a normalization operator reducing a bad property while preserving an invariant, explicitly not Zero), a three-way algebraic/structural/observational Zero taxonomy simpler than the earlier Z0-Z5 hierarchy, an explicit warning that group-level non-additivity (Contr(x,y)=Contr(x)+Contr(y)+I(x,y)) can make Zero(x)=Zero(y)=1 while Zero(x,y)=0, and a confluence/termination framing of repeated Zero-elimination as a route to a genuine canonical reduction theory -- while also surfacing a third distinct 'KR-ALGEBRA-01' naming collision across this batch.

summary: Corrects the record that the Atharva Veda contains no theory of negative numbers (a text search finds no occurrence of 'negative' or 'minus'; 'debt to life' is metaphorical), then builds a rigorous signed-contribution theory: Negative != Zero as a foundational principle, a reference-relative deviation K=B+Delta_B(K), a typed contribution space distinguishing supporting/contradictory/irrelevant/undetermined evidence, a DDD principle that negativity is typed by the invariant it opposes (never an intrinsic property), a preliminary four-valued polarity domain {+,0,-,?}, two distinct kinds of Zero (contribution-Zero vs observational-Zero, not automatically equivalent), a Zero!=Cancellation distinction, and a new prerequisite experiment KR-CONTRIBUTION-01 (Signed Contribution Discovery).
contribution_assessment: Delivers the batch's most careful epistemic-polarity analysis: explicitly falsifies the premise that the Atharva Veda contains negative-number mathematics, then constructs a disciplined signed-contribution theory establishing that 0 != negative and negative != false, that negativity must always be typed relative to a specific invariant/question/utility/representation context (never intrinsic), that a preliminary four-valued polarity domain {+,0,-,?} must not be assumed additive or called an algebra yet, that contribution-Zero and observational-Zero are two distinct notions that need not coincide, that a cancelling pair (C(a)=+1, C(b)=-1) is neutral without either member being individually Zero (a candidate mechanism for higher-order Zero phenomena), and specifies a new prerequisite experiment KR-CONTRIBUTION-01 whose four questions are explicitly expected to show contribution-Zero and observational-Zero do NOT coincide in general -- framed as a valuable separation, not a failure.

summary: Develops the signed-contribution research into an explicit relational/dialectical model (Argument -> Challenge -> Counter-aspect -> Resolution) in which negative contribution is generated relative to an argument, not an independent object, introducing a third Zero concept ('Balance Zero': opposing contributions summing to net-zero equilibrium, distinct from Absence Zero and the established Elimination/Transformation-relative Zero), arguing negative information (a successful challenge) can increase knowledge by revealing an argument's domain boundary, cautioning against literally equating Sunya/Nirvana/Moksha with mathematical zero, and specifying a ten-question research sequence before any Knowledge Algebra claim.
contribution_assessment: Adds a third distinct Zero concept (Balance Zero, C+ + C- = 0 as equilibrium, not elimination or absence) to the prior two, reframes challenge/negative-evidence as knowledge-increasing (revealing an argument's domain boundary rather than merely failing it), explicitly refuses to equate Sunya/Nirvana/Moksha with mathematical zero while preserving the structural analogy as a hypothesis, and crystallizes the key conceptual shift that negative is opposition relative to a reference (not the opposite of existence) and Zero can mean no net effect relative to a reference (not literal nothingness).

summary: Corrects four specific mathematical overstatements in the earlier formal Vedic-Math document (the divisibility-by-4 statistic was not actually minimal, a DPI paragraph was mislabeled, H(D)=n*log2(10) needs a distributional assumption stated, and the '10 Verification Axioms' should be called 'Candidate Structural Properties'), then sharpens the Balance-Zero research: distinguishes Net Balance=0 from Information State is Zero (destroying information by keeping only a net value), freezes a six-term Contribution/Polarity/Composition/Balance/BalanceZero/EliminationZero conceptual ladder, redesigns KR-CONTRIBUTION-01 as eight staged hypotheses (H1-H8), separates Contribution from Challenge in the KR-ALGEBRA signature, and articulates that something negative relative to a claim can be positive relative to overall knowledge growth.
contribution_assessment: Provides concrete corrections to specific overclaims in an earlier document (minimal sufficient statistic, DPI mislabeling, entropy formula's hidden distributional assumption, 'axioms' renamed to 'candidate structural properties'), a critical new distinction (Net Balance=0 vs Information State is Zero -- collapsing a +5/-5 pair into a net 0 destroys information), a staged eight-hypothesis experimental ladder for KR-CONTRIBUTION-01, an explicit separation of Contribution (a value) from Challenge (a relation/process) in the KR-ALGEBRA signature, and the striking epistemological claim that something negative relative to a specific claim (C_claim(B)<0) can simultaneously be positive relative to overall knowledge growth (C_knowledge(B)>0).

summary: Endorses 'purification' as a KnowledgeOS hypothesis (not theorem): a challenge that weakens an argument (C_claim(B)<0) can simultaneously strengthen the knowledge state (C_knowledge(B)>0) by revealing a domain boundary, transforming a claim M into a qualified claim M|C; adds Purification as a third Zero-adjacent concept alongside Elimination Zero and Balance Zero, and proposes the candidate principle 'challenge does not necessarily reduce knowledge; it can purify it' for testing in KR-CONTRIBUTION-01.
contribution_assessment: Sharpens the argument/knowledge contribution split into a concrete transformation Claim+Counterevidence -> Qualified Claim (M becomes M|C), explicitly conditions the negative-to-purifying inference on the challenge being valid, relevant, and successfully integrated (an arbitrary false objection would not purify), and adds Purification as a third distinct Zero-adjacent phenomenon (Elimination Zero: nothing relevant remains from x; Balance Zero: opposing contributions have no net residual; Purification: challenge removes unjustified scope/assumption), noting Zero here is reached after information is added and processed, not because information disappeared.

summary: Reads Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka four-alternatives argument (Asti/Nasti/Ubhaya/Nobhayam) as structural inspiration -- never metaphysics to import -- for a time-indexed knowledge-transition theory: distinguishes three kinds of emptiness (representational, epistemic, relational -- the last being the existing Transformation-relative Zero), argues Zero is both state- and time-relative, reframes K_t->K_{t+1} as a purification process where scope can shrink while validity increases, proposes a knowledge transition algebra KA_T=(K,T,Delta,Gamma,equiv,Pi) with idempotent-purification and non-reversible-revision candidate properties, introduces Empty_{Q,C}(K_t) as distinct from K_t=empty-set, and specifies experiment KR-STATE-TRANSITION-01.
contribution_assessment: Introduces a genuinely new source (Nagarjuna's Madhyamaka four-alternatives argument) used disciplined-ly as structural inspiration, producing several substantive new formal pieces: a three-way representational/epistemic/relational emptiness taxonomy (with relational emptiness identified as exactly the pre-existing Transformation-relative Zero), an explicit time-indexing of Zero (Zero_t(x) != Zero_{t+1}(x)), a purification reframing of knowledge transitions (scope can decrease while validity increases), a knowledge transition algebra KA_T with idempotent-purification (P^2=P) and non-reversibility candidate properties, a question-relative Empty_{Q,C}(K_t) predicate explicitly not implying the knowledge state is the empty set, and a fully specified experiment KR-STATE-TRANSITION-01 with three primary objectives.

summary: Tightens KR-STATE-TRANSITION-01 before freezing: replaces the plain set-difference residue Delta_t=K_t\K_{t+1} with a tripartite (removed/transformed/acquired) residue since qualification is not deletion, argues the residue/justification history matters even when two transitions reach the same endpoint state, adds a fourth 'unresolved' status distinguishing unexamined from inconclusive, makes the status partition non-exclusive (typed tag sets, not mutually exclusive states), redefines purification as challenge-driven qualification-with-preserved-justification rather than removal, splits idempotency into operational versus observational forms, replaces the tau^-1!=K_t hypothesis with a proper reversibility predicate, proposes a transition monoid/category as the deepest candidate object, and finalizes a six-hypothesis (H1-H6) experimental spec plus a concrete JSON transition-record schema.
contribution_assessment: Delivers the mature, implementation-ready version of KR-STATE-TRANSITION-01: a tripartite residue Delta_t=(Delta_t^-,Delta_t^o,Delta_t^+) replacing plain set difference, a 'residue is more important than the difference' principle (same endpoint state can arise from different epistemic histories), a three-level State-emptiness/question-relative-emptiness/transformation-relative-Zero distinction, a fourth Unexamined-vs-Unresolved status split, non-exclusive multi-tag status annotations, purification redefined via challenge-qualification-preservation rather than removal, operational-vs-observational idempotence, a proper reversibility predicate Rev(tau,K_t) replacing an unjustified inverse-inequality hypothesis, a transition monoid/category framing left open between algebra and category theory, a finalized six-taxonomy 'non-being in knowledge systems' table, six core hypotheses H1-H6, and a concrete JSON schema for logging transition records in an actual implementation.

summary: Applies DDD separation of concerns (Question/Claim/Evidence/Challenge/Determination/Revision contexts) to locate where 'Knowledge Sunya' appears: not as an empty claim object but as the absence of context-independent determination, i.e. Status(C)=f(C,Q,Context,E,Standards,t) rather than f(C) alone. Distinguishes Object emptiness, Determination emptiness, and Relational emptiness as a triangle, argues Sunya is a boundary concept between bounded contexts (a relation not established implies no legitimate inference), formalizes hypothesis H-SUNYA-01, and models a Determination->Challenge->Sunya->Revision->New-Determination purification cycle. The file's second half (from 'Yes. I think this is the right next move' onward) duplicates its own first half verbatim.
contribution_assessment: Completes the batch's Zero/emptiness research arc with the most DDD-grounded formulation: Knowledge Sunya is relocated from the claim object into the missing relation (Claim minus Question, minus Evidence, minus Context each destroy a different aspect of determination), a Knowledge Sunya triangle (Object/Determination/Relational emptiness) is fixed as non-equivalent, Sunya is identified as a boundary concept appearing precisely where an inter-context inference (Evidence.supports -> Determination.justified -> Governance.accepted -> True) is not explicitly established, K_t is restructured into seven explicit relational components (claims, evidence, challenges, determinations, questions, revisions, history), and a formal hypothesis H-SUNYA-01 (Relational Epistemic Emptiness) is stated with its two required non-implications (never falsity, never non-existence).
